guest.name: 翔さん
guest.role: Ski instructor in {白馬|はくば}, {健太|けんた}'s snowboarding friend

title_jp: {白馬|はくば}スキー{計画|けいかく}
context: Friday 27 November, evening: {健太|けんた} makes a LINE group to plan a ski day in {白馬|はくば} and adds his friend {翔|しょう}さん, a ski instructor who will teach アルちゃん, who has never skied.
scene: Friday night. {健太|けんた} adds you to a new LINE group with his friend {翔|しょう}さん, a ski instructor. Your first ski day is being planned.

phrases.jp: {板|いた|ski, board|3}、{予約|よやく|reservation, booking|4}しておきますね。
phrases.en: I'll book the skis in advance.
phrases.note: ておく = do it now so it's ready later.

phrases.jp: {雪道|ゆきみち|snowy road|3}を{甘く見ない|あまくみない|to underestimate|3}ほうがいいよ。
phrases.note: Review: {甘|あま}く{見|み}る from the first-snow day + ないほうがいい.

phrases.jp: {寒い|さむい}から、{重ね着|かさねぎ|layering clothes|3}して{行こう|いこう}。
phrases.en: It's cold, so let's wear layers.
phrases.note: Review: {重ね着|かさねぎ}する. Every {長野|ながの} local will tell you this.

phrases.jp: {大雪|おおゆき|heavy snow|3}のため、{電車|でんしゃ}が{遅れて|おくれて|to be late|4}いるらしい。
phrases.en: Apparently the train is late because of heavy snow.
phrases.note: Review: ため (cause) + らしい (hearsay). The winter combo.

phrases.jp: {寝坊|ねぼう|oversleeping|4}しないように、{目覚まし|めざまし|alarm clock|4}をかけておこう。
phrases.en: I'll set an alarm so I don't oversleep.
phrases.note: {目覚|めざ}ましをかける = set an alarm. ておこう = let's do it beforehand.

dialogue_setting: A new LINE group called 「{白馬|はくば}いこ」, made by {健太|けんた} on Friday night.

dialogue.speaker: 健太
dialogue.jp: グループ{作った|つくった}で！{白馬|はくば}スキー{計画|けいかく|plan|3}や🏂
dialogue.en: Made a group! The {白馬|はくば} ski plan 🏂
dialogue.note: Kansai: {作|つく}ったで = {作|つく}ったよ, や = だ.

dialogue.speaker: 健太
dialogue.jp: こっち{翔|しょう}。スキーの{先生|せんせい}やねん。アルちゃんに{教えて|おしえて}くれるって
dialogue.en: This is {翔|しょう}. He's a ski instructor. He says he'll teach you, アルちゃん.
dialogue.note: Kansai: やねん = なんだ.

dialogue.speaker: 翔さん
dialogue.jp: はじめまして！{翔|しょう}っす。{初心者|しょしんしゃ|beginner|3}、{大歓迎|だいかんげい|very welcome|3}っすよ！
dialogue.en: Nice to meet you! I'm {翔|しょう}. Beginners are very welcome!
dialogue.note: っす = です, casual-polite young men's speech.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: よろしくお{願い|ねがい}します！スキーは{生まれて初めて|うまれてはじめて|for the first time in my life|3}です
dialogue.en: Nice to meet you! It'll be my first time ever skiing.

dialogue.speaker: 翔さん
dialogue.jp: {板|いた|ski, board|3}と{靴|くつ}はレンタル{予約|よやく|reservation, booking|4}しとくっす。{手袋|てぶくろ|gloves|3}は{自分|じぶん}で{用意|ようい|preparing|3}しといてください！
dialogue.en: I'll book rental skis and boots. Get your own gloves ready, though!
dialogue.note: しとく = しておく, しといて = しておいて.

dialogue.speaker: 健太
dialogue.jp: {10日|とおか}の{木曜|もくよう}、{朝|あさ}7{時|じ}に{鷹ノ原|たかのはら}{駅|えき}{集合|しゅうごう|meeting up (at a place)|3}な。{寝坊|ねぼう|oversleeping|4}したら{あかん|あかん|(Kansai) = だめ, no good|3}で
dialogue.en: Thursday the 10th, meet at {鷹ノ原|たかのはら} station at 7 a.m. Don't you dare oversleep.
dialogue.note: Kansai: あかん = だめ. {集合|しゅうごう}な = {集合|しゅうごう}ね.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {了解|りょうかい|got it|4}！{目覚まし|めざまし|alarm clock|4}、2つかけとく！
dialogue.en: Got it! I'll set two alarms!

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: でも{転んで|ころんで|to fall over|4}も{笑わないで|わらわないで|to laugh|4}ね…
dialogue.en: But don't laugh if I fall over…

dialogue.speaker: 翔さん
dialogue.jp: {最初|さいしょ|the beginning, first|4}はみんな{転ぶ|ころぶ|to fall over|4}っすよ！{転び方|ころびかた|how to fall|2}から{教える|おしえる}っす！
dialogue.en: Everyone falls at first! I'll start by teaching you how to fall!
dialogue.note: っす = です. Falling safely really is lesson one.

listening.intro: {翔|しょう}さん sends one more voice message about the day.

lines.jp: {山|やま}の{上|うえ}は{寒い|さむい}んで、{重ね着|かさねぎ}してきてくださいっす！
lines.en: It's cold up the mountain, so come wearing layers!

grammar.meaning: do in advance, leave as is
grammar.form: {動詞|どうし}て{形|けい}: + おく ({予約|よやく}しておく, かけておく) · casual: 〜ておく → 〜とく ({予約|よやく}しとく, かけとく) · request: 〜ておいて → 〜といて ({用意|ようい}しといて)
grammar.explanation: Review: you do something now so it's ready for later. Planning chats are full of it: {予約|よやく}しとく, {用意|ようい}しといて. In speech ておく becomes とく, and でおく becomes どく ({読|よ}んどく).

examples.jp: {電車|でんしゃ}の{時間|じかん}、{調べておきます|しらべておきます}ね。
examples.en: I'll check the train times beforehand.

examples.jp: おやつ、{三人分|さんにんぶん}{買っといた|かっといた}よ。
examples.en: I've bought snacks for three already.

quiz.question: {寝坊|ねぼう|oversleeping|4}しないように、{目覚まし|めざまし|alarm clock|4}を＿＿。
quiz.en: I'll set an alarm so I don't oversleep.
quiz.explain: かけておこう shrinks to かけとこう. どく is only after a voiced で ({読|よ}んでおく → {読|よ}んどく).

quiz_more.question: {地図|ちず}、{前|まえ}の{日|ひ}に{読ん|よん}＿＿よ。
quiz_more.en: I'll read the map the day before.
quiz_more.explain: {読|よ}んでおく → {読|よ}んどく: after で, おく becomes どく.

quiz_more.question: ビール、{冷やして|ひやして|to chill|3}＿＿から、{飲んで|のんで}いいよ。
quiz_more.en: I've chilled the beer, so go ahead and drink it.
quiz_more.explain: Done beforehand, ready now → past おいた. おく would mean you haven't done it yet.

kanji.where: On the slope map {翔|しょう}さん sends: the green runs are marked 初級コース.
kanji.breakdown: {初級|しょきゅう}: 初 first + 級 grade, level → 'the first level'.
kanji.related: {中級|ちゅうきゅう} = intermediate, {上級|じょうきゅう} = advanced. Japanese classes use them too.

tip.title: The っす guy
tip.body: っす is a shortened です used by young men, often in sports clubs, with seniors or friends of friends. It's friendly and respectful-ish, but not real keigo: never use it with a boss, a teacher or a customer. Women use it less, though some do as a joke.

challenge.prompt: {翔|しょう}さん: 「{予約|よやく|reservation|4}しといたっす！{10日|とおか}、{楽しみ|たのしみ}にしてるっす！」 You can't wait either. Which sticker?
challenge.explanation: {楽|たの}しみ！ answers {楽|たの}しみにしてる with the same excitement. {怖|こわ}い… would say you're scared, ガーン is shock at bad news, and おやすみ would end the chat.
challenge.hint: He's looking forward to it. Match his mood.

vocab.note: {計画|けいかく}を{立|た}てる = make a plan. Bigger than {予定|よてい} (schedule).
Any flat board. Skiers just say {板|いた} for their skis.
{予|よ} beforehand + {約|やく} promise. {予約|よやく}する = to book.
{手|て} hand + {袋|ふくろ} bag → a bag for your hand.
On schedules: 7{時|じ}{駅|えき}{集合|しゅうごう}. {現地集合|げんちしゅうごう} = meet there.
{寝坊|ねぼう}する = to oversleep. The classic excuse for being late.
Short for {目覚|めざ}まし{時計|どけい}. {目覚|めざ}ましをかける = set an alarm.
Falling while walking or skiing. {落|お}ちる is falling from a height.
{最初|さいしょ}は = at first. Opposite: {最後|さいご} = last.

kanji_study.parts: 宀 roof on top + 丬 a bed seen from the side + the rest a person under the covers → lying in bed under a roof: sleep.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 浸 (soak): 浸 has 氵 water on the left and no roof.

kanji_study.parts: 代 (タイ, gives the sound) on top + 衣 clothing below → a piece of cloth that holds things: bag.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 装 (dress up): 袋 has 代 on top, 装 has 壮.

extras.title: On the slopes
extras.title_jp: ゲレンデの{言葉|ことば}
extras.intro: Words you'll hear on your first ski day.

items.note: From German Gelände. スキー{場|じょう} is the whole resort.
{一日券|いちにちけん} = day pass.
Skiers say {滑|すべ}る, not スキーする, for the actual skiing.

extras.title: Planning in a group chat
extras.title_jp: グループで{予定|よてい}を{決める|きめる}
extras.intro: Short lines for fixing a date with friends.

items.note: Polite: ご{都合|つごう}はいかがですか.

items.jp: {空いてる|あいてる|to be free|4}{日|ひ}ある？
items.note: {予定|よてい}が{空|あ}いてる = no plans.

items.jp: {現地集合|げんちしゅうごう|meeting at the spot|2}で！
items.note: Each person makes their own way.
